title: Bundle credit scenarios — quick calc & experiment notes
content:
Quick back-of-envelope to explore hybrid bundles (credits + PAYG) with seat ties and rollover. Meant for first-pass experiment spec — keep lightweight.

Goal: create 2-3 simple bundle offers that (a) increase ARPU vs pure PAYG, (b) provide predictable revenue for Dedicated/Private conversations, and (c) surface easy upgrade paths. Test on small cohort of PLG signups and in a couple of K-shaped enterprise pilots.

Assumptions (rough):
- Baseline PAYG effective cost to customer: $0.004 per 1k tokens (current list = placeholder)
- Redwood underlying unit cost (inference infra + support amortized): $0.0008 per 1k tokens on averaged workloads (mix of chat/generation + embeddings)
- Target gross margin on hosted: 70%+ for self-serve bundles
- Typical small-app usage: 250k tokens/mo; mid-market: 1M tokens/mo; power app: 5M+ tokens/mo

Bundle idea A — Starter Credits (intent: capture hobby / trial -> paid)
- $19/mo -> 200k generation tokens + 10k embedding units + 1 seat
- Overage PAYG at $3.50 per 1M tokens (i.e. $0.0035 per 1k)
- Effective cost if fully used: $19 / 200k = $0.095 per 1k tokens (note: includes embedding quota so haircuts) -> looks high vs PAYG but positioned as convenience/discount vs list for small usage where PAYG rounding hurts
- Unit econ: revenue per 1k = $0.095, cost per 1k = $0.0008 => gross margin ~99% on these units (obviously weird because per-token calculus for small bundles is not representative; treat as retention lever)
- Upsell trigger: at 400k/mo usage -> recommend Growth bundle

Bundle idea B — Growth Hybrid (intent: net-new ARPU lift)
- $99/mo -> 1.5M generation tokens + 50k embeddings + 3 seats
- Overages at $2.5 per 1M (or $0.0025 per 1k) for tokens; seat add-on $20/seat/mo beyond included
- Effective per-k if fully used: $99 / 1.5M = $0.066 per 1k tokens
- Compare to PAYG at $0.004 per 1k -> This seems backwards: our bundle per-token is higher because bundles sell convenience & seats. Need to re-evaluate sizing so bundle actually gives discount vs PAYG for higher usage.
- Alternative: price $79 for 1.5M -> $0.0526 per 1k. Still higher than baseline PAYG assumption. So adjust assumption: set PAYG list-target ~ $0.08/1k? Need data.

Observation: We need to pick a consistent baseline. Current internal PAYG comps we see in market are ~ $0.01–0.05 per 1k depending on model. My previous $0.004 is low (more like provider-to-provider wholesale). For product positioning, assume list PAYG = $0.03 per 1k.
- Recompute Growth: at $79 / 1.5M => $0.0526/1k -> still a premium. Set Growth to $49 -> $0.0326/1k -> ~par to PAYG; value is seats/embeddings + burst.

Bundle idea C — Team Predictable (intent: reduce churn, get commits)
- $499/mo -> 10M generation tokens + 250k embeddings + 10 seats + priority support
- Overage: $1.5 per 1M ($0.0015 per 1k) up to 50M
- Effective per-1k = $499 / 10M = $0.0499 per 1k -> again depends on where baseline sits
- If baseline PAYG = $0.08/1k then this is 37% discount; if baseline is $0.03 then it's worse. Key: need to align list PAYG and perceived model quality.

Variant: Credit buckets with sliding price bands
- e.g., 0–1M tokens: included at $0.03/1k; 1–5M: $0.015/1k; >5M: $0.0075/1k. Sell bundles that essentially prepay at blended rates to guarantee margin.

Roll-over / expiry policy experiments (impact on economics):
- Option 1: No roll-over. Simpler, encourages consumption or upgrade.
- Option 2: 30-day roll-over up to 50% of monthly quota. Increases perceived value; marginal churn impact uncertain.
- Option 3: Annual prepay: 12x months + 2 months free; roll-over allowed across year. Attractive for sales-assisted accounts.

Seat bundling (common failure mode):
- Seat-based pricing prevents easy mapping for usage-based LLM API. Consider seat+credits hybrid: base seat cost covers product/console access; credits buy tokens. Seat price acts as floor revenue; credits scale.
- Example: $10 seat + credits pool shared. If a team has 5 seats + Growth bundle credits, then ARPU floors to $50/mo + credits revenue. Good for stable revenue but complicates self-serve.

Edge-case: very spiky apps (burst). Offer burst buffer credits that auto-bill at a premium but avoid rate-limited failures: e.g., buffer bucket of 1M burst tokens at 2x PAYG. Could convert to reserved capacity conversation.

Unit-econ quick table (toy):
- Use baseline: list PAYG = $0.03 per 1k; infra cost = $0.0008 per 1k.
- Growth bundle example: $49 for 1.5M => revenue per 1k = $0.0326; gross margin = (0.0326 - 0.0008)/0.0326 ~ 97.5% (again inflated because each bundle has fixed admin costs not included).
- More realistic: allocate $10 infra fixed overhead per account + variable token cost. For cohort of 1k accounts, fixed overhead amortized small. Need real cohort modeling.

Experiment plan (small, 6–8 week):
- A/B rollout on new signups (only newbies) with 3 arms: PAYG baseline, Starter bundle ($19+credits), Hybrid Growth ($49+credits). Track conversion to paid, 30/60/90-day retention, ARPU at 30/90 days, avg tokens/mo, overage rates.
- Success criteria: increase 90-day ARPU by 20% and no >10% increase in churn vs PAYG.
- Secondary: collect qualitative feedback in checkout flow "why did you pick this?"

Tracking metrics we need at high fidelity:
- tokens_used_by_account (30d, 90d)
- credits_consumed_vs_included (counts of accounts that hit cap)
- overage_revenue (sum)
- ARPU (30d/90d) and median tokens per paying account
- upgrade_rate from starter->growth in 90 days

Open questions / TODOs:
- Reconcile what we call "1k token" units vs embedding units (embeddings charged differently). Need to standardize on documentation and pricing table.
- Get baseline actual PAYG datapoints from billing team (Luis) for last 6 months: median/75/95 percentile tokens/account.
- Determine legal/finance constraints on roll-over credits and refunds.
- Define gating for Dedicated sales: at what monthly committed tokens threshold do we surface Dedicated contract? (e.g., >50M tokens/mo or >$X committed revenue)

Notes to self: write a short pricing copy that emphasizes predictability + seats for teams, credits for usage, and burst protection. Keep 2–3 simple SKUs in self-serve (Starter, Growth, Team) and keep enterprise/Reserved separate.

Random rough numbers for discussion meeting:
- Ask: if average usage of Growth cohort is 700k tokens/mo but they bought 1.5M, what's churn signal? low (bundle overage unused) vs high (wasted credits). Might still be net positive because prepaid revenue.
- Important to model churn vs prepaid exhaustion: does prepay reduce churn (sunk cost) or increase churn (wasted credits + dissatisfaction)? historical SaaS suggests small prepaids reduce churn.

Slack ping plan: poke Luis for billing slices + Maya for product copy. Then draft experiment page in Confluence and a short linear ticket to implement variant A on checkout.

End of notes — will iterate after pulling billing tables.

-- Asha
